# Results — Study 789 (SUE Earnings-Surprise Drift)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**post-earnings-announcement drift lines up with standardized unexpected earnings** (SUE): sort
names on SUE at each filing, and the top-minus-bottom forward 1–3-month return spread should be
positive (Bernard & Thomas 1989). Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete
calendar month; the partial current month is dropped, and any event whose drift window would run
past the as-of is excluded). Fingerprint `4d0fd3625f76` (basket adjusted closes, as-of-sliced).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **adjusted** closes for a fixed **30-name** large-cap basket, 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-30 (5,406 rows) |
| Fundamentals | EDGAR XBRL `companyconcept` **diluted EPS** (frame-tagged calendar quarters, with the 10-Q/10-K **filing date**), basic EPS as the rare fallback |
| Surprise | **SUE** = seasonal-random-walk surprise `EPS_q − EPS_{q−4}` divided by the rolling std of the **last ~8** such seasonal differences known strictly before `q` (Foster-Olsen-Shevlin 1984 / Bernard-Thomas 1989) |
| Events | **1,315 / 1,279 / 1,261** usable (ticker, filing-date) events at the 21 / 42 / 63-day horizons, over 30 names, filed **2012-07-26 → 2026-06-03** (each print needs ≥8 prior seasonal surprises before a SUE is emitted; EDGAR framed EPS starts ~2012 for this basket) |
| Execution / lag | one documented convention: anchor at the first session **on/after** the filing date, **enter the close one day later** (signal known at the filing, return earned from t+1), hold H ∈ {21, 42, 63} trading days |
| Costs | one-way × per-event turnover (4 × one-way on a long-short round trip) + short-leg borrow at 50 bps annualised over the hold |
| Adjustment | **total-return** (adjusted closes) throughout |

**Survivorship, named on the Signal axis.** The basket is 30 names *still trading in 2026* — a
survivor set. A current-membership panel tilts the long leg mildly upward (blow-ups are absent),
but it can point *against* a drift as easily as for it; and the whole PEAD family is documented to
concentrate in **small, illiquid** names (Chordia et al. 2009), so a large-cap survivor basket is
exactly where the textbook drift is *weakest*. This is a deliberately conservative test.

## The headline — forward drift of a top-minus-bottom SUE tercile long-short

| horizon | n | top tercile | bottom tercile | **long-short** | one-sample *t* (naive) | **calendar-time Newey-West *t*** | win-rate (Wilson) | right-tail placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 21d (~1mo) | 1,315 | +1.06% | +2.22% | **−1.16%** | −2.29 | **−1.41** | 50.6% [47.3, 53.9] | 0.991 |
| 42d (~2mo) | 1,279 | +1.70% | +3.47% | **−1.77%** | −2.48 | **−0.41** | 46.9% [43.6, 50.3] | 0.995 |
| 63d (~3mo) | 1,261 | +3.34% | +4.29% | **−0.95%** | −1.12 | **+0.41** | 48.9% [45.5, 52.3] | 0.879 |

The long-short is **the wrong sign at every horizon** — the *top*-SUE names drift *less* than the
*bottom*-SUE names (a mild reversal, not a drift). The naive one-sample *t* is significantly
*negative* at the short horizons (−2.29 / −2.48), but that statistic is inflated by the seasonal
clustering of filings; the autocorrelation-robust **calendar-time Newey-West *t*** (aggregating the
long-short into ~50 earnings-season buckets) is **statistically nothing** in either direction (max
magnitude 1.41, and only +0.41 at the canonical 3-month PEAD horizon). The right-tail
label-shuffle placebo confirms no *positive* drift (p = 0.88–0.99).

## Monotonicity — quintile drift, low → high SUE

A real PEAD rises monotonically from the bottom SUE quintile to the top. It does not:

| horizon | Q1 (low SUE) | Q2 | Q3 | Q4 | Q5 (high SUE) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 21d | +2.04% | +1.91% | +0.89% | −0.05% | +1.74% |
| 42d | +3.37% | +3.49% | +2.48% | +0.03% | +2.69% |
| 63d | +3.91% | +4.48% | +4.10% | +1.16% | +4.42% |

The pattern is **non-monotone** — the *lowest* SUE quintile is among the *highest*-drifting, the
4th quintile is a trough, and the relationship has no consistent slope. There is no "buy the top,
short the bottom" gradient to trade.

## The sign flips with the bucket count (a hallmark of no real signal)

At 63d the tercile long-short is **−0.95%** (*t* = −1.12) but the *decile* long-short is
**+1.53%** (*t* = +0.99) — opposite signs, neither significant. A robust anomaly does not reverse
its sign when you re-slice the same sort into a different number of buckets. Together with the
non-monotone quintiles, this is the classic signature of noise, not signal.

## Within-quarter block placebo (respects the earnings-season clustering)

Shuffling SUE labels only *inside each calendar quarter* — the null that respects the seasonal
clustering — the observed long-short is unremarkable: block-placebo *p* = **0.84 / 0.91 / 0.63** at
21 / 42 / 63 days. Nothing to rescue.

## The cost test — long-short net of costs (63d)

| cost (one-way) | gross long-short | net long-short |
|---|--:|--:|
| 5 bps | −0.95% | **−1.27%** |
| 10 bps | −0.95% | **−1.47%** |

There is no gross edge to erode; net of realistic costs and borrow the long-short is simply more
negative. Nothing to deploy.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased and well-powered

Deterministic price panel + SUE events with a TUNABLE planted post-earnings drift; no network.

| world | long-short *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.08** (sd 0.57), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted edge = 0.08 (seed 789) | long-short **+16.60%**, **t = +21.50** |

The detector never fires on the null and lights up strongly on a planted drift — so the flat
real-tape result is a genuine *absence* of signal on this basket, not a broken pipeline. *(A
faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Sorted on SUE, the top-minus-bottom drift is **the wrong sign** at 1–3
  months (−1.16% / −1.77% / −0.95%); the autocorrelation-robust calendar-time Newey-West *t*
  **never clears 2** in the predicted direction (max **+0.41** at 63d); the cross-section is
  **non-monotone** and the sign **flips between terciles and deciles**; the within-quarter block
  placebo sits at p = 0.63–0.91 and the right-tail label-shuffle placebo at p = 0.88–0.99. The
  synthetic control (0/20 nulls fire; planted t = +21.5) proves the detector works. The classic
  Bernard-Thomas SUE drift **does not replicate** on this 30-name large-cap survivor basket.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Gross is negative and net of costs (−1.27% to −1.47% at 63d) more
  negative still. There is nothing to deploy.
- **Does the textbook PEAD replicate here? — BUSTED.** Non-monotone quintiles, a sign that flips
  with the bucket count, and a robust *t* pinned near zero: the standardized-unexpected-earnings
  drift is absent on liquid large-cap survivors — exactly where the literature (Chordia et al.
  2009; McLean-Pontiff 2016) predicts it should be weakest or gone.
